questions.question: What is the primary role of <!DOCTYPE html> at the beginning of an HTML file?
options: To inform the browser to render the page in modern HTML5 standards mode
To import external JavaScript libraries automatically
To encrypt user cookies for cybersecurity compliance
To establish a persistent WebSocket connection to the server
questions.hint: It prevents the browser from switching into legacy Quirks Mode.
questions.explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> instructs modern web browsers to parse the page using the HTML5 specification and avoid legacy Quirks Mode.

questions.question: Where should the <title> tag be placed in an HTML document?
questions.hint: The title is metadata displayed in the browser tab.
questions.explanation: The <title> element is metadata and must reside inside the <head> section.

questions.question: What is the purpose of <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">?
options: It enables responsive mobile design by setting the viewport width to match device width
It restricts the webpage to desktop monitors only
It automatically loads external fonts from Google Fonts
It disables zooming and screen readers for accessibility
questions.hint: Think of mobile devices and responsive rendering.
questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag ensures that mobile browsers render pages matching the physical device width at a 1:1 scale instead of zooming out.

questions.question: Which character encoding is the web standard specified by <meta charset="UTF-8">?
questions.hint: It supports international characters and emojis.
questions.explanation: UTF-8 is the universal standard encoding for the modern web, covering virtually all Unicode characters and symbols.

questions.question: Which tag contains all the visible elements that users see and interact with?
questions.hint: The body holds all headings, paragraphs, and components.
questions.explanation: The <body> element houses all visible UI content rendered in the browser window.
